newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends on highs, prepares for RB statement.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends on highs, prepares for RB statement.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar staged a late flurry on Asian buying to end firmly on Friday as the market prepared for next week's monetary policy statement from the Reserve Bank.
The kiwi was closing at US$0.7012/19 and 66.86 on its Trade-Weighted Index, from 0.7008/15 and 66.81 in the morning.
A dealer said the currency was pushing higher in a market that was still somewhat short. He saw it testing 0.7020 overnight, while 0.6995 should hold on the downside.

A chief dealer said the market was correcting from aggressive selling after Tuesday's coalition announcement between the National and New Zealand First parties, which included the appointment of populist NZ First leader Winston Peters as Treasurer.
He said there had been some good Asian buying and short-covering towards the end of the week.
"I don't think we're in the midst of a major move higher -- I think it's more a case of the market feeling that we've come (down) a little bit too far too quickly," he said.
The focus was now switching to the RBNZ statement on Tuesday. Economists expect this to sanction the easing which has already occurred, but doubt whether it will go further.

"I think that will again confirm there's relatively limited upside for the New Zealand dollar in the medium term. I don't think this is the start of a big move up. I think this is just a correction, a consolidation phase before we begin a more sustained move lower," the chief dealer said.
